summary: Intermittent 401s in private deployment after token-swap: azp vs aud mismatch during service account exchange
description:
Issue summary: Nimbus Labs reported intermittent 401 Unauthorized errors for scheduled batch jobs and short-lived admin API calls after we rolled their private deployment changes last week. Impact: A subset of service-to-service token exchanges fail validation causing retries and job backlogs for their nightly worker fleet. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) in us-west, private control plane. Authentication flow affected: SAML->OIDC bridge + internal service-account token-swap that issues access tokens with 'azp' (authorized party) set but 'aud' (audience) omitted or set to a short list; our authz layer validates 'aud' and rejects tokens where expected audience is missing.

High level: Customers see intermittent 401s with message 'token audience mismatch' when worker instances try to call model-serving endpoints. Errors started shortly after Nimbus applied an upstream identity provider change (IdP started returning azp only for certain service assertions).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger the scheduled batch worker that performs service account token-swap via the customer's IdP through the bridge proxy
2) Observe token issued by token-swap endpoint (inspect id_token/access_token claims), note presence of 'azp' claim and either missing or unexpected 'aud' claim
3) Call the protected admin/model endpoint with the swapped token; endpoint returns 401 with 'aud mismatch' error in logs
4) Repeat during high concurrency window to reproduce intermittent failure (rate/parallelism appears to correlate).
logs: 2026-03-10T02:14:23Z identity-proxy: token-swap success for svc_worker_42, access_token claims: {"azp":"idp-client-7", "exp":1710000000}
2026-03-10T02:14:24Z authz: token validation failed: required_audience="redwood-inference-api" actual_audience=null (azp=idp-client-7) -> 401
2026-03-11T03:05:11Z serving-runtime: incoming request from svc_worker_42 rejected 401 token_aud_mismatch (x-request-id=abc-123-def)
2026-03-12T08:22:44Z identity-proxy: intermittent 502 from upstream idp during assertion fetch (retry 2)
investigation: Support triaged and confirmed 401 pattern with Nimbus engineering via Zoom session 2026-03-10.
Confirmed a correlation between high-concurrency token-swap activity and increased 401s (reproducible in customer's load test harness).
Captured example tokens (redacted) where 'azp' is present but 'aud' is either missing or set to an array with a single element that does not match our expected 'redwood-inference-api' audience.
Hypothesis 1: IdP/bridge started emitting tokens where 'aud' is omitted and relying on 'azp' for audience semantics; our authz validator is strict and only checks 'aud'.
Hypothesis 2: Under concurrency, token-swap service occasionally returns a legacy token format due to a race in token-builder code path (local IdP proxy cache stale).
Collected telemetry: authz rejects spike corresponds to periods where the idp-proxy returned tokens with atypical claim sets.
Edge case: Some long-lived admin API calls succeed because they use cached tokens with correct aud; short-lived swapped tokens fail.
Added temporary log hooks to identity-proxy and authz to log claim sets for failed validations (sanitized).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Notified Nimbus POC and requested token samples + IdP change log. Asked for scope of affected worker fleet.
2026-03-10 11:45 - Nimbus Eng (customer): Provided sample tokens and noted they rolled an IdP change the night before that adjusts audience behavior for service clients.
2026-03-11 02:05 - Riley Nguyen (SRE): Reproduced locally using customer's sample token; authz library rejects when aud==null. Opened INT-2054 to track authz validator enhancement.

2026-03-12 16:30 - Eng on-call (Ivan Petrov): Confirmed token-swap sometimes returns tokens from fallback code path without aud when upstream responded with 202+retry; submitted PR to identity-proxy to normalize aud claim. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/198
2026-03-13 09:00 - Nimbus Ops: Applied temporary workaround on their IdP to include a static aud claim for service assertions while we patch the bridge.

2026-03-14 07:22 - Riley Nguyen (SRE): Deployed hotfix to identity-proxy in customer's private control plane to populate aud when missing (maps azp -> expected aud). Monitoring shows error rate drop from 3.8% -> 0.1% over 1h.
2026-03-14 12:00 - Aisha Patel (Support): Notified customer and scheduled postmortem call to finalize follow-ups and docs updates. Marking incident as In Progress until verification window completes.
root_cause: Identity-proxy token-swap edge case: under certain upstream responses the token builder emitted access tokens lacking the 'aud' claim, while downstream authz strictly validated 'aud' only. An IdP change increased frequency of that code path, making failures intermittent under load.
workaround: Temporary workaround applied by Nimbus Ops: include static 'aud' in IdP assertions. We deployed an identity-proxy hotfix in the private control plane that synthesizes the expected 'aud' when absent (maps from azp).
resolution: Hotfix deployed to customer's private control plane (identity-proxy v1.8.3-hotfix). The patch normalizes token outputs: if 'aud' is missing, set aud to configured service audience derived from azp mapping. Post-deploy monitoring for 24 hours shows error rates back to baseline. Customer confirmed scheduled workers resumed normally.
postmortem_followups: 1) Merge PR #198 into main and add unit + integration tests for aud/azp normalization (INT-2054).
2) Update Runbook: 'Token Exchange - aud/azp validation' with mitigation steps and verification commands.
3) Add metric and alert: authz.token_aud_mismatch_rate per-customer and per-region to Console (owner: SRE).
4) Documentation: add guidance for private customers on IdP audience configuration and expected claim sets.
5) Schedule a 1:1 with Nimbus to review long-term plan for token semantics; offer optional managed mapping configuration in Private Console.
notes: Customers using private deployments who perform token-swaps should ensure their IdP includes aud matching the expected service audience. We will relax authz validator to accept aud derived from azp only after careful testing and opt-in for strict customers.
estimated_impact: Approximately 5% of scheduled batch runs for Nimbus Labs across us-west during peak windows were affected prior to mitigation. No data loss reported; retries increased job latency.
